Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

ahead adverb

in front, on before the others

also go on ahead, go ahead of, run ahead, send ahead, lead the way

classical

Cic. Rep. 2.55: ut singulīs cōnsulibus alternīs mēnsibus līctōrēs praeīrent

praeeō, praeīre, praeīvī (praeiī), praeitum

verb, irregular (a compound of eō), with the dative of the person · Conjugation on Wiktionary

go ahead, go in front, lead the way

Latin puts “ahead” into the verb with prae-: praeīre, go ahead; praecurrere, run ahead; praemittere, send ahead.

Other words

  • ī prae (abī prae) — go on ahead (I’ll follow)

    also used · classical · Ter. And. 171b: Ī prae, sequar.; Plaut. Amph. 543b–544: Abī prae, Sōsia, jam ego sequar.

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter. (Lewis & Short: the adverb prae is ante-classical))

  • praecurrō, praecurrere, praecucurrī, praecursum — run ahead

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Hec. 371: ūna illārum intereā properē praecucurrit; Plaut. Merc. 223b: quīn ea ego hūc praecucurrī grātiā · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • praemittō, praemittere, praemīsī, praemissum — send ahead

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 602: ā portū mē praemīsistī domum; Caes. BC 1.39.2: Caesar legiōnēs in Hispāniam praemīserat · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Examples

  • Abī prae, Sōsia, jam ego sequar.

    Go on ahead, Sosia; I’ll follow in a moment.Plaut. Amph. 543b–544

  • nam ut dūdum ante lūcem ā portū mē praemīsistī domum

    for when you sent me on ahead from the harbour, home, before dawnPlaut. Amph. 602

See also in front of, forward, straight on, ahead.

SourcesLewis & Short: praeeo · Lewis & Short: prae · Lewis & Short: praecurro · Lewis & Short: praemitto

Plautus, Terence, Cicero and Caesar checked against the Perseus Latin texts; the Amphitruo farewell is also in the Latinitas loci collection (loci-plautus).
